nary_nodes.label: Russian attack on Kyiv
evidence: Ukraine’s capital Kyiv came under a deadly Russian attack early Monday morning

Massive explosions lit up the night sky as ballistic missiles and drones hammered parts of the city, killing at least 19 people in the city and eight others in the surrounding region, with dozens more wounded, officials said.

nary_nodes.label: Russian attack on Kyiv last Thursday
evidence: the fresh assault comes just days after a ferocious Russian attack on Kyiv killed 30 people last Thursday – the third-deadliest attack on the capital since the war began.

nary_nodes.label: NATO summit in Turkey
evidence: on the eve of a critical NATO summit in Turkey that US President Donald Trump plans to attend.

nary_nodes.label: Trump-Putin call
evidence: Trump then offered again to help end the war on Sunday during a nearly 90-minute call with Russian President Vladimir Putin, according to Russia’s foreign ministry.

Russia’s war in Ukraine will form the backdrop to the NATO summit this week in Turkey, where Trump will meet with Zelensky. The pair spoke on the phone on Saturday.

nary_nodes.label: Ukrainian strike on oil refinery
evidence: On Monday, the Ukrainian military said it struck Russia’s largest oil refinery, in a long range strike more than 2,500 kilometres from the Ukrainian border.

nary_nodes.label: Power outages in Ukraine
evidence: Monday’s attacks led to power outages across a number of regions in Ukraine, including Kyiv, Sumy, Kharkiv and Dnipropetrovsk, the country’s electricity transmission agency said.

evidence: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky had warned just hours earlier that Moscow was “preparing a new massive strike,”

nary_nodes.label: UN statement on casualties
evidence: Civilian casualties in 2026 are “significantly higher” than during the same period in 2025, the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine said in a Monday statement.

nary_nodes.label: Zelensky plea for missiles
evidence: Ahead of the summit, Zelensky is using the attacks on Kyiv to renew his plea for allies to supply Ukraine with missiles for Patriot systems.

nary_nodes.label: Zelensky on interceptor shortage
evidence: The “insufficient supply of interceptor missiles” was the reason Ukraine was unable to shoot down any ballistic missiles in Monday’s assault, Zelensky said in a statement.

nary_nodes.label: von der Leyen on air defence
evidence: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said that the country “urgently needs more air defence. We will discuss it this week in Ankara at the @NATO Summit.”

nary_nodes.label: Russia defense ministry statement
evidence: Russia’s defense ministry said it used “high-precision, long-range weapons” to target military-industrial facilities and fuel and energy sites in Kyiv on Monday. It said the attacks were in response to Ukrainian attacks on civilian infrastructure in Russian territory.

nary_nodes.label: Zelensky on Putin's timing
evidence: “This is typical of Putin: right after America’s Independence Day and before the NATO Summit in Ankara,” Zelensky said Sunday in a post on X ahead of the attack.

nary_nodes.label: TASS report on drones
evidence: Russia shot down 519 Ukrainian drones launched toward it overnight into Monday, the state news agency TASS reported.

nary_nodes.label: Ukraine's drone campaign
evidence: it comes as Russia is suffering a major fuel crisis amid Ukraine’s campaign of drone strikes on its energy infrastructure.

nary_nodes.label: Russia's advance in Donetsk
evidence: Russian forces have also stepped up efforts to take more of Ukraine’s eastern Donetsk region – a key objective for the Kremlin, and Ukraine’s cities face near-nightly attacks from Moscow’s drones and missiles.

nary_nodes.label: Ukrainian attacks on Russian infrastructure
evidence: Ukraine, meantime, has also recently ramped up missile and drone attacks against key infrastructure deep inside Russian territory, including oil refineries, ports and military factories.

nary_nodes.label: Rescue operations in Kyiv
evidence: Rescuers evacuated residents, including children, from the upper floors of a damaged building in the district early Monday , while many in the capital spent hours in air raid shelters.

nary_nodes.label: Zelensky on Patriot missiles
evidence: “As long as Patriot missiles remain in our allies’ stockpiles, Russia is only encouraged to keep ‘vanquishing’ residential buildings,” he added.

nary_nodes.label: Zelensky on air defense decisions
evidence: “It is critically important that the world – first and foremost the United States and our European partners – come out of the NATO Summit in Ankara with strong decisions in support of our air defense,” he said

nary_nodes.label: Zelensky on Patriot capabilities
evidence: Zelensky sees Patriots as key for shooting down Russia’s arsenal of ballistic missiles, loitering munitions and increasingly its Geran-4 jet-powered drones –– which fly too fast for Kyiv’s mobile fire groups and can only be shot down with ground-to-air missiles or fighter jets.

nary_nodes.label: Air force data on strikes
evidence: None of the ballistic missiles fired at Ukraine on Monday were shot down by air defenses, according to data from its air force, which said 29 ballistic missiles and 18 attack drones had struck 34 locations across the country. More than 350 drones and 66 missiles were launched toward Ukraine, with Kyiv the main target, it said.

nary_nodes.label: Klitschko on destruction
evidence: There was “destruction and damage” in four districts of the city, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said, adding that the Podilsky district was hit the hardest.

nary_nodes.label: Zelensky on war resolution
evidence: The US president had vowed to solve the war within 24 hours of taking office for a second time, but more than 500 days into his current term, the administration has yet to find a path to peace between the neighbors, despite multiple attempts.
